title: plans/<id>.json
description: One retirement scenario (PLANNER.md). Amounts are yearly, in today's money (real terms), in the library's base currency, and after income tax: income from work and pensions is entered net, and the plan computes only the taxes of tax. Only id, name, retirement and spending are required; a section left out takes its defaults, and the app leaves out sections and lists that are empty.

id.description: The same as the file name, and the name of the plan's projections/<id>/ folder.

age.description: The age work stops: retiring at an age means stopping work on that birthday, or on the start date if it has passed. "earliest" lets the planner find the earliest age that reaches the confidence level. At most endAge (error planner.retirementAge).

endAge.description: The last age the plan must fund. Default 95; above your age and at most 120 (error planner.endAge).

tax.description: The only taxes the plan computes, set by hand.

investmentRate.description: The tax on investments, as a fraction ("0.26"): on the gain part of every sale from the money you can draw, and every year on the income its classes pay out (assumptions.returns.<class>.incomeYield), paid the following year. Required for the plan to run (error planner.investmentRate); "0" when investments aren't taxed. From 0 to 0.9.

wealthRate.description: A yearly tax on the money you can draw above wealthAllowance, as a fraction ("0.002"). Accounts available only from a later age aren't counted until they open. Default 0; from 0 to 0.1 (error planner.wealthRate).

wealthAllowance.description: What the wealth tax leaves untaxed. Default 0; not negative (error planner.wealthAllowance).

work.description: Working phases. Every phase stops at retirement, whatever its until.

contributions.description: Payments into specific accounts, such as a pension fund. They come out of the year's savings; the rest goes to the money you can draw.

events.description: One-off amounts. At most 64 can be uncertain (error planner.uncertainEvents).

runs.description: The number of Monte Carlo runs. Default 2000; from 1 to 10000 (error planner.runs).

seed.description: The random seed; every run of the plan uses the same draws, so differences come from your changes. Default 1.

confidence.description: The share of simulated futures that must succeed for a "yes". Default "0.9"; above 0 and below 1 (error planner.confidence).

phaseEnd.description: A date, or "retirement", which follows the retirement age.

name.description: Default "Work", or "Work 2" when there are several.

until.description: The phase's last day, or retirement. Not before from (error planner.workDates).

netIncome.description: What reaches your account in a year, after income tax and social contributions. Required for the plan to run (error planner.noNetIncome); plans migrated from a gross amount lack it until it's entered.

realGrowth.description: Yearly growth of the income above inflation, as a fraction. Default 0.

spending.description: Yearly spending. Savings are what's left of income after spending.

phases.description: Factors on retirement spending from given ages: the latest phase started is in force, 1 before the first.

flexibleSpending.description: A guardrails rule that cuts retirement spending after bad years and restores it after good ones, never below a floor (PLANNER.md, Flexible spending). Absent: retirement spending is fixed in real terms. { "enabled": true } is the rule with the defaults. Every share is a fraction of the plan's spending; what's left out takes the default. Out-of-range settings are an error while the rule is on (planner.flexibleSpending).

enabled.description: false turns the rule off and keeps its settings in the file. Default true.

cut.description: How much a cut, or a raise, moves the spending level. Default "0.1"; above 0, at most 1.

floor.description: The lowest the level goes: the essentials. A run succeeds while spending is never forced below it. Default "0.8"; from 0 to 1.

upperGuardrail.description: How far the withdrawal rate may rise above the first retirement year's, as a share of it, before spending is cut. Default "0.2".

lowerGuardrail.description: How far it must fall below the first year's, as a share of it, before a cut is restored. Default "0.2".

pension.description: A pension from your pension statement, after tax, kept in real terms. Paid from the birthday at fromAge (part of a year in the year it starts); one starting after endAge is never paid (warning planner.pensionAfterEnd).

fromAge.description: The age it starts at. Required for the plan to run (error planner.pensionAmount).

perYear.description: The yearly amount after tax. Required for the plan to run (error planner.pensionAmount).

contribution.description: Every year while working (perYear, until until), or once (amount in year). One into an account the plan doesn't count is left out (warning planner.contributionOutsidePlan). Not negative.

perYear.description: The yearly amount. Left out for a one-off amount.

until.description: When yearly contributions stop. Default retirement.

amount.description: A one-off amount, paid in year, instead of perYear.

year.description: The calendar year of a one-off amount. Default: the plan's first year.

event.description: A one-off amount, at an age or in a year (exactly one of the two).

amount.description: Positive for a windfall, negative for an expense; after any tax on it.

probability.description: The chance it happens, default "1". Each Monte Carlo run draws whether it does; the deterministic run includes it from 0.5.

portfolio.description: Where the plan starts and the mix it rebalances to.

start.description: The check-in the plan starts from: "latest-check-in" (the default) or a date.

exclude.description: Accounts left out, besides those with includeIn.plan false and closed ones.

unrealizedGainShare.description: The estimated share of value that's gain, for holdings without a recorded costBasis. Without it their whole value counts as gain (warning planner.unknownCostBasis).

targetMix.description: The mix the money you can draw is rebalanced to every year, from today. Left out: it's rebalanced back to its own mix at the start. A mix that doesn't add up to 1 is scaled (warning planner.targetMixTotal).

targetMixByAge.description: Changes of the target mix with age. Each year's target is the mix of the last step in the list that has started by the age reached that year; before any has, targetMix. Ages given as numbers must go up (error planner.targetMixAges); a retirement step can be anywhere.

fromAge.description: An age, or "retirement": the year work stops, for whatever retirement age the planner tries.

inflation.description: Yearly inflation, as a fraction. It only matters for taxes: what you paid stays in the money of the day, so inflation counts as gain when sold. Default "0.02"; from -0.5 to 0.5 (error planner.inflation).

returns.description: Each asset class's yearly real return, net of fund costs. A class left out takes the default: by their median, equity 5% at 17% volatility, bonds 1.5% at 6%, cash 0.5% at 1%, gold 1% at 15%, crypto 0% at 70% (PLANNER.md, Returns).

correlations.description: Correlations between classes' returns, as nested objects: { "equity": { "bonds": "0.1", "crypto": "0.4" } }. One direction is enough. A pair left out takes its default: equity–bonds 0.1, equity–crypto 0.4, other pairs 0. A table that isn't positive definite is repaired (warning planner.correlationsRepaired).

returnAssumption.description: A log-normal yearly real return, given by its mean (real) or its median (medianReal), with its volatility. With gross mean A, gross median g and volatility σ, g = A² / √(A² + σ²). A return given by its median is written with real too, the mean it implies to 6 decimals; when the two disagree, real wins (warning planner.meanAndMedian).

real.description: The arithmetic mean, as a fraction.

medianReal.description: The median, the typical year, which a portfolio rebalanced every year compounds at.

volatility.description: The standard deviation of yearly returns.

incomeYield.description: The share of the value paid out as income each year (dividends, interest): part of the return, not extra, and taxed every year at tax.investmentRate. Left out: income counts as growth, taxed when sold.
